name: datasketch_hll
description: Aggregate input values into a HyperLogLog sketch for distinct counting. Returns a `sketch_hll` BLOB you can persist, ship between processes, or merge later. The first argument is `lg_k` — base-2 log of the number of buckets — which controls the size/accuracy trade-off. `lg_k = 12` (4096 buckets, ~4 KB sketch, ~1.6% standard error) is a common default; raise it for tighter bounds, lower it for smaller sketches. An optional third argument picks the register encoding: `'HLL_4'` (the default, smallest), `'HLL_6'` or `'HLL_8'` (largest, fastest to update); it must be a constant, and parallel combines keep the chosen encoding.

examples.description: Approximate distinct users (lg_k = 12, ~1.6% error)
examples.code:
SELECT datasketch_hll_estimate(datasketch_hll(12, user_id)) AS distinct_users
FROM events;

examples.description: Build per-day sketches and persist them
Build with 8-bit registers and check the encoding

name: datasketch_hll_estimate
description: Read the estimated distinct count from an HLL sketch. Returns a `DOUBLE` — the cardinality estimate.

name: datasketch_hll_union
description: Merge multiple HLL sketches into one. Aggregate over a column of `sketch_hll` BLOBs to roll per-partition or per-day sketches up to whatever window you need — without rescanning the underlying rows. The leading `lg_k` argument is the precision of the output sketch. An optional third argument (`'HLL_4'`, `'HLL_6'` or `'HLL_8'`) sets the encoding of the result. To union just two sketches in a row-wise expression, use the scalar `datasketch_hll_merge`.

examples.description: Rolling 7-day distinct users from per-day sketches

name: datasketch_hll_lower_bound
description: Lower bound of the HLL distinct-count estimate at a given number of standard deviations.

name: datasketch_hll_upper_bound
description: Upper bound of the HLL distinct-count estimate at a given number of standard deviations.

name: datasketch_hll_merge
description: Scalar union of two HLL sketches — the row-wise counterpart of the `datasketch_hll_union` aggregate (the scalar is named `_merge` because a scalar and an aggregate cannot share a name). The result keeps the first sketch's target type; the union runs at the larger `lg_config_k` of the two, and if either input is in dense (HLL) mode the result is reduced to the smaller one.

examples.description: Users seen in January or February, from two stored sketches
examples.code:
WITH a AS (SELECT datasketch_hll(12, user_id) AS s FROM events_jan),
     b AS (SELECT datasketch_hll(12, user_id) AS s FROM events_feb)
SELECT datasketch_hll_estimate(datasketch_hll_merge(a.s, b.s)) AS jan_or_feb
FROM a, b;

name: datasketch_cpc
description: Aggregate input values into a Compressed Probability Counting sketch — a distinct-count sketch that's roughly 40% smaller than HLL at the same accuracy, traded against slower serialization. Choose CPC when you store many sketches at rest and reads are infrequent. The leading `lg_k` controls the size/accuracy trade-off the same way it does for HLL.

examples.description: Distinct-count with CPC
examples.code:
SELECT datasketch_cpc_estimate(datasketch_cpc(12, user_id)) AS distinct_users
FROM events;

name: datasketch_cpc_estimate
description: Read the estimated distinct count from a CPC sketch.

name: datasketch_cpc_union
description: Merge a column of `sketch_cpc` BLOBs into one rollup sketch — the standard per-partition / per-day rollup pattern. For a scalar union of two sketches in the same row, use `datasketch_cpc_merge`.

name: datasketch_cpc_merge
description: Scalar union of two CPC sketches — the row-wise counterpart of the `datasketch_cpc_union` aggregate. The result uses the smaller `lg_k` of the two inputs.

examples.description: Users seen in January or February
examples.code:
WITH a AS (SELECT datasketch_cpc(12, user_id) AS s FROM events_jan),
     b AS (SELECT datasketch_cpc(12, user_id) AS s FROM events_feb)
SELECT datasketch_cpc_estimate(datasketch_cpc_merge(a.s, b.s)) AS jan_or_feb
FROM a, b;

name: datasketch_theta
description: Aggregate input values into a Theta sketch — the distinct-count family that supports set operations (union, intersect, A-not-B) beyond simple merge. The optional leading `lg_k` (4–26, default 12) is base-2 log of the nominal sketch entries. Accepts signed and unsigned integers, floats and VARCHAR; passing a `sketch_theta` (or a BLOB of serialized sketches, e.g. read back from Parquet) merges sketches instead, growing to the largest `lg_k` of the inputs unless one is given. Keyword options: `seed :=` (hash seed — sketches can only be combined with sketches built from the same seed) and `p :=` (up-front sampling probability in (0, 1]). Results are stored in the compressed compact format (serial version 4) when it applies; versions 1–4 are all readable.

examples.description: Build per-cohort sketches
examples.code:
SELECT cohort,
       datasketch_theta(12, user_id) AS sketch
FROM events
GROUP BY cohort;

examples.description: Roll per-cohort sketches up into one (merge aggregate)
examples.code:
SELECT datasketch_theta_estimate(datasketch_theta(s)) AS uniques
FROM (SELECT datasketch_theta(12, user_id) AS s FROM events GROUP BY cohort);

examples.description: Custom seed and sampling probability

name: datasketch_theta_estimate
description: Read the estimated distinct count from a Theta sketch.

name: datasketch_theta_union
description: Approximate `|A ∪ B ∪ …|` — scalar union of two or more Theta sketches. The result keeps the largest `lg_k` inferred from the inputs (at least the default 12); pass a leading `lg_k` (`datasketch_theta_union(16, a, b)`) to set it explicitly. To merge a whole column of sketches across rows, use the `datasketch_theta(sketch)` aggregate.

examples.description: Users in any of three cohorts
examples.code:
WITH a AS (SELECT datasketch_theta(user_id) AS s FROM events_jan),
     b AS (SELECT datasketch_theta(user_id) AS s FROM events_feb),
     c AS (SELECT datasketch_theta(user_id) AS s FROM events)
SELECT datasketch_theta_estimate(datasketch_theta_union(a.s, b.s, c.s)) AS any_cohort
FROM a, b, c;

name: datasketch_theta_intersect
description: Approximate `|A ∩ B|` — distinct items present in both cohorts. The classic use case is funnel and retention analysis: how many users in segment A also appear in segment B, computed from the sketches alone. Accepts two or more sketches; use `datasketch_theta_intersect_agg` to intersect a column of sketches across rows.

examples.description: Retention — users active in Jan AND Feb

name: datasketch_theta_a_not_b
description: Approximate `|A \ B|` — distinct items present in A but not in B. Useful for churn (in-Jan, not-in-Feb) and new-user (in-Feb, not-in-Jan) measurements directly from sketch state.

name: datasketch_theta_get_seed
description: Alias of `datasketch_theta_seed_hash`: returns the 16-bit seed hash stored in the sketch (it always returned the hash, not the seed).

examples.description: Users present in every month
examples.code:
SELECT datasketch_theta_estimate(datasketch_theta_intersect_agg(s)) AS in_every_month
FROM (SELECT datasketch_theta(12, user_id) AS s FROM events_jan
      UNION ALL
      SELECT datasketch_theta(12, user_id) FROM events_feb);

examples.description: How similar are the January and February audiences?
examples.code:
WITH a AS (SELECT datasketch_theta(12, user_id) AS s FROM events_jan),
     b AS (SELECT datasketch_theta(12, user_id) AS s FROM events_feb)
SELECT datasketch_theta_jaccard(a.s, b.s).estimate        AS jaccard,
       datasketch_theta_similarity_test(a.s, b.s, 0.3)  AS at_least_30pct
FROM a, b;

examples.description: Distinct raw payloads
examples.code:
SELECT datasketch_theta_estimate(datasketch_theta_blob(country_code::BLOB)) AS distinct_payloads
FROM page_views;

name: datasketch_tuple
description: Aggregate `(key, value)` rows into a Tuple sketch (`sketch_tuple_double`): a Theta sketch of the distinct keys in which every retained key carries a DOUBLE summary of its values. `mode :=` combines a key's values — `'sum'` (default), `'min'`, `'max'` or `'one'` (presence only). The optional leading `lg_k` (4–26, default 12) sets the nominal size, and `seed :=` / `p :=` work as for `datasketch_theta`. NULL keys or values are skipped. Passing a `sketch_tuple_double` merges sketches (keeping the inputs' `lg_k` unless one is given); the mode is not stored in the sketch, so pass the same `mode :=` when merging.

examples.description: Distinct customers and their revenue from one pass
examples.code:
SELECT datasketch_tuple_estimate(s) AS customers,
       datasketch_tuple_sum(s)      AS revenue,
       datasketch_tuple_mean(s)     AS revenue_per_customer
FROM (SELECT datasketch_tuple(customer_id, amount) AS s FROM orders);

examples.description: Keep each customer's largest order instead of the sum
examples.code:
SELECT datasketch_tuple_mean(datasketch_tuple(customer_id, amount, mode := 'max')) AS avg_largest_order
FROM orders;

examples.description: Merge per-region sketches
examples.code:
SELECT datasketch_tuple_sum(datasketch_tuple(s)) AS total_revenue
FROM (SELECT region, datasketch_tuple(customer_id, amount) AS s FROM orders GROUP BY region);

examples.description: Customers in both segments, with their combined revenue
examples.code:
WITH a AS (SELECT datasketch_tuple(customer_id, amount) AS s FROM orders WHERE region = 'north' AND customer_id < 30),
     b AS (SELECT datasketch_tuple(customer_id, amount) AS s FROM orders WHERE region = 'north' AND customer_id >= 10)
SELECT datasketch_tuple_estimate(datasketch_tuple_intersect(a.s, b.s)) AS in_both,
       datasketch_tuple_sum(datasketch_tuple_intersect(a.s, b.s))      AS revenue
FROM a, b;

name: datasketch_aod
description: Aggregate `(key, values DOUBLE[])` rows into an array-of-doubles Tuple sketch (`sketch_aod`): a Theta sketch of the distinct keys where each retained key carries a fixed-length array of DOUBLE values (1–255 values, the same length on every row, inferred from the data and stored in the sketch), summed element-wise per key. The optional leading `lg_k` (4–26, default 12) and `seed :=` / `p :=` work as for `datasketch_theta`. Passing a `sketch_aod` merges sketches. Combining sketches with different numbers of values or different seeds is an error.

examples.description: Distinct customers with per-customer revenue and item totals
examples.code:
SELECT datasketch_aod_estimate(s)     AS customers,
       datasketch_aod_column_sums(s)  AS totals,
       datasketch_aod_column_means(s) AS per_customer
FROM (SELECT datasketch_aod(customer_id, [amount, items]) AS s FROM orders);

examples.description: Use the keys with the Theta functions
examples.code:
SELECT datasketch_theta_estimate(datasketch_aod_to_theta(datasketch_aod(customer_id, [amount]))) AS customers
FROM orders;

name: datasketch_frequent_items
description: Aggregate input values into a Frequent Items (heavy-hitter) sketch. The optional first argument is `lg_max_k` (default 10) — log₂ of the maximum number of tracked items, so `8` → up to 256 candidates, `12` → up to 4096. Bigger values track more candidates and tighten the per-item error bound. Valid values are 3–30 (anything else is rejected at bind time); typical values run 4–12. FLOAT and DOUBLE items are keyed by their shortest round-trip spelling (the same text as `CAST(x AS VARCHAR)`), so nearby values such as `0.1234567` and `0.1234568` stay distinct.

examples.description: Top countries by page views

name: datasketch_frequent_items_get_frequent
description: Return the heavy-hitter candidates with per-item estimate, lower bound, and upper bound. The second argument selects the error mode: `'NO_FALSE_POSITIVES'` returns only items that are *definitely* heavy (every returned item really is frequent); `'NO_FALSE_NEGATIVES'` returns the union of all candidates that *might* be — every truly-frequent item is included, plus some that may not be.

name: datasketch_frequent_items_estimate
description: Estimated frequency for a specific item. FLOAT/DOUBLE probes are formatted like `CAST(x AS VARCHAR)`; sketches of FLOAT/DOUBLE items built by older extension versions used six-decimal keys and should be rebuilt from source data.

name: datasketch_frequent_items_weighted
description: Like `datasketch_frequent_items`, but each row adds a weight (`BIGINT` or `UBIGINT`; negative weights are rejected) instead of a count of one — approximate top-K by a metric such as revenue or bytes. The optional leading `lg_max_k` (log₂ of the maximum number of tracked items, default 10, valid range 3–30) works as in `datasketch_frequent_items`.

examples.description: Regions by revenue

name: datasketch_kll
description: Aggregate input values into a KLL quantile sketch. Best balance of accuracy, speed, and size — the modern default for general-purpose quantile estimation. The first argument `K` controls accuracy: higher K → smaller error and bigger sketch. `K = 200` is a sensible production starting point. Accepts every numeric type and VARCHAR (strings are ordered bytewise and give a `sketch_kll_varchar`).

examples.description: p50 / p95 / p99 latency from one KLL sketch
examples.code:
WITH agg AS (
  SELECT datasketch_kll(200, latency_ms) AS sketch FROM requests
)
SELECT datasketch_kll_quantile(sketch, 0.50, true) AS p50,
       datasketch_kll_quantile(sketch, 0.95, true) AS p95,
       datasketch_kll_quantile(sketch, 0.99, true) AS p99
FROM agg;

name: datasketch_kll_quantile
description: Approximate quantile at a given rank — given a sketch and `r ∈ [0, 1]`, returns the value at that rank in the sorted distribution.

name: datasketch_kll_rank
description: Inverse of `datasketch_kll_quantile` — given a value, return its approximate rank `r ∈ [0, 1]` in the sorted distribution.

name: datasketch_kll_cdf
description: CDF over a list of split points — one call returns the cumulative rank at each. Useful for histograms. The list has one more entry than there are split points (the last is always 1.0). Always returns `LIST(DOUBLE)` regardless of the sketch's item type.

name: datasketch_kll_pmf
description: PMF (probability mass) over a list of split points — fraction of the distribution falling in each bucket. Always returns `LIST(DOUBLE)` regardless of the sketch's item type.

examples.description: Several quantiles in one call
examples.code:
SELECT datasketch_kll_quantiles(datasketch_kll(200, latency_ms), [0.5, 0.9, 0.99], true) AS p50_p90_p99
FROM requests;

examples.description: Fraction of requests at or under 100 / 500 / 900 ms
examples.code:
SELECT datasketch_kll_ranks(datasketch_kll(200, latency_ms), [100, 500, 900], true) AS ranks
FROM requests;

examples.description: Unnest the retained items with their weights

name: datasketch_tdigest
description: Aggregate input values into a t-digest quantile sketch — most accurate at the tails (p99, p999), exactly where SLOs live. FLOAT/DOUBLE input only. The first argument controls the centroid budget; larger sketches give tighter tail estimates.

examples.description: Tail latency

name: datasketch_tdigest_quantile
description: Approximate quantile at a given rank from a t-digest sketch.

name: datasketch_tdigest_rank
description: Approximate rank of a value within the t-digest sketch.

name: datasketch_tdigest_min_value
description: Exact minimum value seen by the t-digest.

examples.description: Exact range of the readings

name: datasketch_tdigest_max_value
description: Exact maximum value seen by the t-digest.

name: datasketch_req
description: Aggregate input values into a Relative Error Quantile sketch. Error scales with rank rather than being a fixed fraction of `n` — predictable accuracy on highly skewed distributions where a fixed-error sketch over- or under-spends precision at the extremes. An optional third argument `hra` (a constant, default `true`) picks high-rank accuracy (best for p99-style tails); pass `false` for low-rank accuracy. Merging starts from the first input's mode; mixing HRA and LRA sketches is an error.

examples.description: Low-rank-accuracy sketch for the bottom of the distribution

name: datasketch_req_quantile
description: Approximate quantile at a given rank from a REQ sketch.

name: datasketch_req_rank
description: Approximate rank of a value within the REQ sketch.

name: datasketch_req_cdf
description: CDF over a list of split points — the cumulative rank at each split point, plus a final 1.0. Always returns `LIST(DOUBLE)` regardless of the sketch's item type.

name: datasketch_req_pmf
description: PMF (probability mass) over a list of split points — the fraction of the distribution falling in each bucket. Always returns `LIST(DOUBLE)` regardless of the sketch's item type.

examples.description: Several quantiles in one call
examples.code:
SELECT datasketch_req_quantiles(datasketch_req(12, latency_ms), [0.5, 0.9, 0.99], true) AS p50_p90_p99
FROM requests;

examples.description: Confidence interval (2 standard deviations) around the 0.99 rank
examples.code:
WITH s AS (SELECT datasketch_req(12, value) AS sk FROM measurements)
SELECT datasketch_req_rank_lower_bound(sk, 0.99, 2) AS lo,
       datasketch_req_rank_upper_bound(sk, 0.99, 2) AS hi
FROM s;

name: datasketch_quantiles
description: Aggregate input values into the classic mergeable quantiles sketch from the original DataSketches paper. Solid general-purpose choice supporting all numeric input types; for new projects prefer `datasketch_kll`, which gives the same merge semantics with better accuracy/size trade-off. Also accepts VARCHAR items (ordered bytewise, `sketch_quantiles_varchar`).

name: datasketch_quantiles_quantile
description: Approximate quantile at a given rank from a classic Quantiles sketch.

name: datasketch_quantiles_rank
description: Approximate rank of a value within the classic Quantiles sketch.

name: datasketch_quantiles_cdf
description: CDF over a list of split points — the cumulative rank at each split point, plus a final 1.0. Always returns `LIST(DOUBLE)` regardless of the sketch's item type.

name: datasketch_quantiles_pmf
description: PMF (probability mass) over a list of split points — the fraction of the distribution falling in each bucket. Always returns `LIST(DOUBLE)` regardless of the sketch's item type.

examples.description: Several quantiles in one call
examples.code:
SELECT datasketch_quantiles_quantiles(datasketch_quantiles(128, latency_ms), [0.5, 0.9, 0.99], true) AS p50_p90_p99
FROM requests;
